title: task edit's flag names diverge from task create's for the same fields (--label/--reference vs --labels/--add-reference)
description:
Reported by lore-cli (2026-09-14), against quest-cli 0.6.0, while filing tasks in their own repo. A usability/missing-capability gap, not a defect in what exists.

quest task create accepts --label (repeatable, appends) and --reference. quest task edit rejects both outright and instead wants --labels (plural, takes a JSON array) and --add-reference (singular, repeatable). Minimal repro, exit 2 each:

  quest task edit <id> --label release --actor a --actor-kind delegated-agent --accountable-human b
  quest task edit <id> --reference "text" --actor a --actor-kind delegated-agent --accountable-human b

lore-cli's suggestion: either --label on edit should work as an append (matching create's semantics), or the usage error should say "unknown flag --label; did you mean --labels or --add-label?" -- the second is the cheaper fix and does not require reconciling create/edit's differing semantics (create sets initial state; edit's add-*/remove-* pattern is deliberate for list mutation, per the edit-batch and checklist-position conventions elsewhere in this CLI).

This is a good match for the format value-shape work QCLI-266 already did for --acceptance-criteria et al.: the fix belongs wherever flag-name suggestions or the manifest's per-flag metadata already live, not as a one-off special case for --label/--reference.

acceptanceCriteria.text: quest task edit --label or --reference either succeeds (matching an equivalent add semantic) or fails naming the correct flag name to use instead, tested via a real exit-2 repro
quest manifest --json for task edit either lists label/reference under aliases, or the usage/help text for task edit makes the create/edit naming split explicit rather than silent
bun run check exits 0 including new test coverage for the corrected behavior

plan: 1. Reproduce the real exit-2 refusal for `quest task edit --label` and `--reference` and record exactly what it names today.

2. Make the refusal NAME the correct edit-side flags to use instead (--add-label/--remove-label/--labels for label; --add-reference/--remove-reference for reference), with NO alias added (DEC-172 (4ak)).

3. Make the task edit help text and the task edit manifest NAME the create/edit naming split explicitly (create: --label/--reference; edit: --labels/--add-label/--remove-label/--add-reference/--remove-reference).
4. Add a regression test via a real exit-2 repro asserting the refusal names the correct flags, plus a test that help/manifest name the split.
5. PATH-prefix the pinned bun 1.4.2 (ambient is 1.3.14, QCLI-471) and confirm bun run check exits 0.
implementationNotes: Implemented QCLI-283 per DEC-172 (4ak): task edit with --label or --reference now exits 2 naming the edit-side flags (--labels / --add-label / --remove-label; --add-reference / --remove-reference); no alias added. The refusal also carries the discard sentence, so nothing was written.

AC-2 second arm done: the task edit help summary names the CREATE/EDIT NAMING SPLIT explicitly. The task edit manifest entry also gained an additive, non-alias refusedFlags map naming both sides, so quest manifest --json names it too.

AC-3 evidence: pinned bun 1.4.2, bun run check exits 0 (typecheck, lint, format:check, layer:check, 1143 tests pass, 46 mod tests pass; NOT TYPECHECKED pre-existing). New suite test/qcli283-edit-create-flag-split.test.ts, 6 tests. Head 81adfd74 on branch qcli-283-edit-label-refusal; tree clean.

DEC-172 (4aq) A1 correction: the refusedFlags manifest field was DROPPED (commit 9ae2b39c); the create/edit split is named in the help only, with no new manifest field, and exit 2 naming the edit-side flags is the machine-readable signal. The refusedFlags note above is superseded by this ruling.
